paragraphs: I'm Rahul Krishnan, a Data Science master's student at Universitaet Trier and a former SAP software developer with over 4 years of professional software engineering experience at SAP Labs India. I build AI systems end to end, from training and evaluation through to containerised deployment, and I am drawn to the engineering layer that decides whether a model actually ships: latency, memory, cost and reliability.

My MSc thesis addresses a core bottleneck in long-context LLM inference, the memory consumed by the KV cache. Its public preprint reports 2x to 3x near-lossless KV cache compression, with quality preserved on reasoning and long-context retrieval: https://arxiv.org/abs/2607.12550. Around it I have studied where LLMs can be trusted, from chain-of-thought faithfulness on BIG-Bench Hard to reward design for calibration and selective abstention. On the applied side I have shipped a RAG assistant on Google Cloud Run, a Two-Tower recommender on Azure, and a neuro-symbolic model for cross-lingual narrative similarity.

I care about results that hold up: multi-seed evaluation, honest error bars and measured latency over single-run headline numbers. My interests sit at the intersection of LLM inference efficiency, evaluation and alignment, recommender systems, and reliable MLOps.
